dossier.architecture: Trench-capable drum with passive flexible hopper roof after early bump-only configuration.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module specification unresolved here.
subsystems.intake: Two-roller intake with pin/slot hopper retraction for agitation.
subsystems.transfer: Seven floor rollers with tape flaps; slotted transfer rollers allow compression adjustment.
subsystems.scoring: High-inertia two-motor launcher; shooter orientation reversed to avoid turning after pickup. Flexible Hopper Flopper compresses beneath trench and re-expands for capacity.
subsystems.controls: Transfer speed responds to shooter speed error to balance recovery and accuracy; revised autonomous routes exploit trench access.

versions: Space City to Farmersville/DCMP changed roof and shooter orientation.
Tape-flap improvement reported as roughly 18–20 to 25–30 BPS; independent measurement not available.
dossier.analysis: Route access can outrank additional storage: being beaten to neutral fuel motivated trench clearance. A flexible roof aims to preserve capacity while recovering that route, with retention and collision behavior becoming essential tests.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-9128 · Trench access and speed-error feeding explain the rebuild
context_documents.body:
# 2026-9128: Trench access and speed-error feeding explain the rebuild

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A slotted three-roller transfer provides adjustable compression before a two-X60 high-inertia launcher. The flexible Hopper Flopper compresses under the trench and re-expands afterward. The shooter was reversed relative to the original robot, and the feeder speed varies with launcher speed error. The interview explicitly reports no climb.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links trench access to losing neutral-zone fuel races, preserving capacity to avoiding a smaller fixed hopper, and reversed orientation to reducing the need to turn after acquisition. Transfer modulation is intended to give fuel sufficient energy transfer while maintaining accuracy.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A compliant storage envelope changes which routes are available, so its value cannot be measured only in added fuel. It can change autonomous arrival order and the opponent’s available supply. Speed-error-dependent feed is a form of demand management: slow entry when the launcher is behind instead of allowing a nominally high feed command to create low-energy misses. The caption’s flywheel mass arithmetic is inconsistent, so preserve the qualitative high-inertia claim and seek a published mass breakdown rather than silently choosing one number.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare route arrival times, full-load trench passage, recovery after contact, and total scored fuel with fixed versus variable feeding. Measure sustained and initial BPS separately.

## Limits

Interview plus team replies in topic 515730. The first release reports about 15–16 BPS over a full roughly 80-fuel hopper versus around 20–25 initially; these are team reports for that configuration, not measurements of every later revision.

source_reviews.title: ITKAN Triple Threat and Retrial recap
source_reviews.review_basis: Read complete team-authored post text from Discourse JSON
source_reviews.facts: Team reports roughly 80 fuel, 15–16 BPS across emptying and 20–25 BPS initially in the earlier account. Recap identifies defense and trench access as reasons for Retrial.
source_reviews.limitations: Team estimates with no shot conversion or timing protocol. Keep estimates scoped to the early account.

source_reviews.title: ITKAN 2026 public robot code
source_reviews.review_basis: Read downloaded Java source and README
source_reviews.facts: Command averages both shooter measurements for duty calculation, begins on either side reaching its threshold, latches feeding, and gates transfer duty on alignment.
source_reviews.limitations: Public code cannot authenticate match software or physical roller geometry.

source_reviews.title: ITKAN Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Existing interview synopsis and fresh caption retrieval attempt
source_reviews.facts: Prior corpus describes slotted transfer, reversed shooter and a high-inertia launcher.
source_reviews.limitations: Full captions unavailable in this pass. The retained synopsis flags inconsistent flywheel mass arithmetic.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: ITKAN’s Triple Threat and Retrial illustrate a route-driven change to a drum scorer. The team says that the first event exposed a defense problem and that it adopted a passive variation on Citrus Circuits’ hopper to retain a high inventory while using the trench. Its early hopper-emptying claim also distinguishes the beginning of a burst from full discharge. The released code gives a separate view of the same system: movement compensation chooses a shot and feed demand depends on measured launcher speed, but physical transfer is also gated by chassis alignment. The configuration and software evidence come from different publications.
piece_flow: The deployable intake acquires from the floor. The released project has separate conveyor and transfer outputs between the intake and shooter.
The retained dossier describes a three-roller transfer with adjustable compression. The release command starts the conveyor funnel while waiting for alignment and applies transfer duty once aligned.
The drum launches a wide stream. ITKAN’s published initial volley rate exceeded its hopper-emptying average for the early robot.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Retrial’s passive Hopper Flopper allows the storage envelope to yield under the trench. Loading, side hits and repeated rubbing can all change the effective envelope. The old interview synopsis reports a reversed shooter orientation, a useful hypothesis for reducing post-pickup chassis rotation that the inspected recap does not describe. The released trench alignment command combines lateral correction and heading alignment while preserving driver translation.

subsystems.name: Hopper and access
subsystems.operation: Yield under the trench and restore storage volume afterward.
subsystems.team_rationale: Defense limited the useful scoring route at the first event.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Test the actual passing envelope with fuel pressing upward under the roof, since empty clearance alone does not prove the route.
subsystems.interfaces: Roof folds near fuel, moving collector hardware and approach clearance.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check repeated abrasion, side misalignment and whether roof deformation persists after contact.
subsystems.unknowns: Roof stiffness, net material and retention at different fill states.

subsystems.name: Transfer and launch
subsystems.construction: Separate conveyor and transfer software interfaces. Physical roller arrangement comes from retained synopsis.
subsystems.operation: Drive transfer only when aligned, with duty scaled by averaged speed ratio and bounded from 0.5 to 1 for positive targets after entry.
subsystems.team_rationale: Earlier team reply distinguished sustained flow from launch burst.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A speed average can mask one lagging side and the minimum duty can still overload a weak launcher. Compare by side and by load.
subsystems.interfaces: Drive alignment, launcher velocity and funnel activity enter the same release sequence.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect for fuel packed against a paused transfer while the funnel continues running.
subsystems.unknowns: Lane geometry, drive alignment tolerance in match and actual shots per battery condition.

revisions: Triple Threat was the first competition release.
After Space City #1 the team developed Retrial with the passive Hopper Flopper to improve route access under defense.
The public robot code is a later snapshot with no confirmed event binary mapping.
transferable_principles: Measure both access to contested fuel and scored output from that fuel when comparing clearance strategies.
Treat speed-dependent transfer as a controller across physical subsystems. Launcher recovery, transfer duty and alignment should be logged together.
Measure full-load discharge and last-fuel behavior separately from the first second.
disconfirming_conditions: A low fixed roof can be preferable if a compliant roof drags, rebounds into the drum, or spills enough fuel to erase the route gain.
If neither launcher side can sustain release speed under simultaneous drive and feed, continuous reduced feed can still produce low-energy misses.
remaining_gaps: No fresh readable interview captions, measured roof deflection, complete discharge traces or verified hardware pairing for the public software snapshot.
recommended_images: Reveal thread post 12, Triple Threat and Retrial views. Add a side-on loaded roof clearance sequence if available.
